metanarrative_source: HyperNorm metanarrative from established WSA authoring context. Original English biographies and calls are design proposals.

records.name: Ned Seatbell
records.biography_en: In The Long Order of Business, Ned Seatbell takes the role of presiding officer. “The bell has the floor.”
records.frizzlebob_note_en: FrizzleBob's field report: little bell with a padded striker held close.

records.name: Mara Minutehand
records.biography_en: In The Long Order of Business, Mara Minutehand takes the role of cabinet minute taker. “I'll record the silence as present.”
records.frizzlebob_note_en: FrizzleBob's field report: tiny open blank notebook and a short blunt pencil.

records.name: Theo Floorclaim
records.biography_en: In The Long Order of Business, Theo Floorclaim takes the role of backbench speaker. “My point is nearly short.”
records.frizzlebob_note_en: FrizzleBob's field report: compact handheld speech token with a sculpted upward arrow.

records.name: Otto Rubberstamp
records.biography_en: In The Long Order of Business, Otto Rubberstamp takes the role of senior civil servant. “It arrived in triplicate.”
records.frizzlebob_note_en: FrizzleBob's field report: one chunky date stamp with a blank base and tied paper slip.

records.name: Ivy Fileturn
records.biography_en: In The Long Order of Business, Ivy Fileturn takes the role of registry clerk. “File under almost done.”
records.frizzlebob_note_en: FrizzleBob's field report: two tiny file jackets joined by an oversize removable clip.

records.name: Perry Queuecode
records.biography_en: In The Long Order of Business, Perry Queuecode takes the role of public service desk officer. “You're number next.”
records.frizzlebob_note_en: FrizzleBob's field report: small spool of blank queue tickets with one exposed ticket.
